recipes.name: Country Chicken Casserole
ingredients_raw: 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cut into bite size pieces
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Stir hash browns and 1/2 of the onions together in a 9x13 inch baking dish, then lay cheese slices on top and layer chicken over cheese. In a small bowl, mix soup and milk together and pour mixture over chicken.

Bake in preheated oven for 30 to 35 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and juices run clear. Pour corn onto chicken and stir to combine all ingredients, then bake for an additional 20 minutes.
Sprinkle remaining onions over all and bake for another 5 minutes, or until onions are golden brown. Let sit 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Country Chicken Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Chicken breast, hash browns, fried onions and cheese. Now that's country cookin' for ya! This is a wonderful easy recipe, especially if want a filling meal, but don't have time to stay in the kitchen. This is my mother-in-law's favorite dish, and it heats up well for leftovers.

review.reviewBody: I made this for dinner tonight with a few adjustments. I used 5 cups of hashbrowns and baked them for crispiness before adding the rest of the ingredients. I added the corn into the soup mixture, I used 2 cans of soup and 2 cups of milk. I used shredded Colby/jack cheese. This was good. Next time I think I will use more potatoes, and more cheese. My pickey children even liked it.

I've made this a few times now, and it turns out great every time. This is my new go-to dish when I have leftover rotisserie chicken. I like to pre-cook my hash browns, use whatever shredded cheese is in the fridge and frozen corn instead of canned. It's really easy to change the flavors by adding garlic or even curry powder. I did find that a full can of French-Fried onions was too much, a half can is sufficient.

This is definitely going into our dinner roster. It is amazing, although I tweaked it just a little. I used pre cooked chicken strips and a can of corn with bell peppers and mixed that right in with the hashbrowns with some salt and pepper. I also used a can of cheesy broccoli soup and cream of chicken soup. I topped the chicken with real bacon pieces and used shredded cheese. Baked in the oven for 50 minutes. The last 10 minutes I topped with the fried onion pieces. Delicious!!

My family loved this recipe! My son and husband are picky eaters so I am very happy to have a comfort meal we all loved. I precooked 3 chicken breasts in chicken broth, then cut up and added to the mixture of 4 cups potatoes, soup (I used cream of chicken AND cream of mushroom) 1 1/5 soup cans of milk, lots of shredded Mexican cheese and 16 oz. frozen corn. I did not add any onions to the mix. I mixed all this up, then baked 55 minutes, added 2-3 oz. French fried onions and baked another 5 minutes. There's no way we would have eaten it with 6 oz. of onions. Served with dinner rolls and a salad, this was perfect. 17 year old son said it was one of his favorite recipes that we've tried! Definitely a keeper for us.

I layered the hashbrowns (added seasoned salt and pepper), a good handful of the french fried onions, shredded Monterrey jack cheese, chicken (which I cooked with chicken seasoning), and corn (only used about 2/3 can). I used cream of mushroom soup, mixed it with the milk and poured it over the entire casserole. Baked it all for 50 minutes - came out perfectly. My husband and I liked the variety of textures and the combination of the flavors.

I made this today. I cooked a whole chicken in the crock pot and used the meat and chicken stock added mixed veggies and cream of chicken soup and hash browns and cheddar cheese and topped with pieces of bread all over the casserole. Then baked it and it is Wonderful! Tastes like chicken pot pie. SOOOOO GOOOOD! It's not mushy at all and has a very good consistently!

I really liked this recipe. I made some changes, however, and it turned out great! I mixed the chicken, soup, milk, corn, some green onions and fried onions together first. I then seasoned the mixture with garlic powder, onion salt and pepper. I fried the hashbrowns so they were a bit crispy and warmed through. I layered the hashbrowns first, spread sliced velveeta over the top of the hashbrowns, then poured the mixture on top of that. I baked and topped with more fried onions as directions stated. It was really yummy. Will definitely do this one again!

So comfort and delicious! Used frozen hashbrowns, can of cream of celery(all I had handy)and added 1/2 cup sour cream when I added corn to mix...other than that, followed directions to a tee, and it was wonderful!!! Oh yeah...did take the chicken out for 5 minutes at the end and broiled the rest to brown potatoes a bit...my husband loves the crispy stuff! Super comfort food!!! No need to cook hashbrowns first if you follow the directions...even if they are frozen.

This is so good. We are in the middle of a snow storm and this was the perfect meal to come in from the cold to. I used a bag of the Ore-Ida crispy crowns instead of hashbrowns and omitted the onions because my husband doesn't like onions (bummer).I precooked half the bag of crispy crowns, added the chicken and the rest of the ingredients and baked for 35 minutes then added the corn and topped it with the rest of the crispy crowns and baked until they were golden brown. Awesome stuff !!!

I loved this! I used russet potatoes, shredded in place of the frozen hash browns and slices off of mild cheddar block because I didn't realize I was out of American cheese. I also seasoned chicken with garlic, onion, and pepper. Had a duh moment and completely forgot the layer of corn, instead adding shredded cheese with the remaining French-fried onions on top. Yum!!! Thank you!

My whole family loved this dish. I did add some garlic salt and black pepper. Didn't realize until I went to make it that I was out of corn! Also, I didn't have a large can of french fried onions, only 1 of the small cans and I think this was the perfect amount. I did not add any of the onions to the hash browns, simply put them on top for the last 10 minutes of baking time. I cooked for 35 minutes, added onions and cooked for an additional 10 minutes. For those of you who complain about the hash browns being soggy... this is a casserole type dish, they are meant to be slightly soggy. If the original author wanted it to have crispy hash browns, he would have told you to cook them seperately and then use the chicken mixture as a topping. We loved it, will definately make it again and try to remember the corn next time! = )
Quick to put together. Used frozen corn, about a cup. Poultry seasoning as a touch, used skinless thigh meat.
It was amazing!
Making this for almost 20 years now. Always a family favorite!!
Omitted corn and used shredded mild cheddar instead of American cheese. Served with green beans. Easy to assemble and great comfort food. Husband said it was a keeper!
I’ve been making the recipe for years and love it! It taste good fresh and as left overs.

I used cubed hash browns because I had exactly 3 cups to use up. I only had half the french fried onions because I wanted to keep it healthier so I didn't have any for the top. The second time I made this my 9 yr old did not like it and I just thought it was ok. I didn't have enough fried onions, maybe that would have helped. I did add green peppers and wish I hadn't. Normally I like them in everything but they didn't do well in this.
I made this casserole for my granddaughter and a few of her friends. They loved it. All of the teens went looking for more and asked me to make again soon.
I would not put anything on top of it.
Not much flavor, needs more seasoning. Also, not good as leftovers
